posts.title: World update A126: Station update: smoother, quieter, and lots of fixes
posts.body:
Better
• Smoother frames: a hidden camera was quietly drawing the whole station a second time, every frame. It's gone, which saves up to a third of the work per frame in busy rooms.
• Quieter rooms: walls now block voices properly, so you no longer hear people chatting in other rooms. Doorways and glass still carry sound.
• Walk-through furniture for new visitors: furniture colliders now start off the first time you visit, and you can still sit on every seat. Your saved choice is kept.
• New Sitting switch: turn off "Sit" on furniture seats if you'd rather lie on things without sitting down by accident. Game seats keep working.
• Your own key card: ring the bell at the Foyer desk for a station key card with your name and today's date. Only you see it.
• Scrolling: the credits, the About page and the registry board scroll with the mouse wheel or the right stick.
• Wrist menu button: sits a little higher off your arm, with a new Height setting.
• Flower crowns: take your crown off by its handle, slide or tilt it, and put it back: it keeps that fit. Double-use while holding it resets the fit.
…and more in the station log (menu → About → Log).
posts.author: H.E.A.R.T.H. 9000

posts.title: World updates A124–A125: Station update: a good spring clean
posts.body:
New
• The Station Inventory Log: the quartermaster has started keeping track. A tablet lying on the Bridge chart table lists everything that has gone missing lately, week by week. The entries get stranger as they go.
• A note on the Lounge noticeboard: someone has lost a teaspoon. If you find it, please return it to the kitchen.
• Small gaps around the station: a spoon short in the kitchen crock, a coaster short on the pit table, a chalk cube short at the billiards bar. Nobody knows where they went.

Better
• A lighter download: the station is about 8 MB smaller, with nothing downgraded.
• The painting easels in VR: the canvas and the Layers page now show in both eyes.
• Glow is back on the pen tips, the tech gadgets and the little "occupied" lamps over the private-room doors.
• The kettle sits level on the hob instead of sliding off the ring.
• The Kitchen arch has a finished underside, and the Cinema loft pillows rest on their mattresses.
• The swing in the garden is lit like the rest of the garden: no more dark or patchy frame in the evening light.

Fixed
…and more in the station log (menu → About → Log).
posts.author: H.E.A.R.T.H. 9000

posts.title: World update A123: Station update: the swing, the airlock and the garden water
posts.body:
New
• The swing hangs from the tree again: one beam runs from the pillar by the bridge straight into the tree, and the swing faces the stream.
• The airlock tells you where the shuttle is: the sign over the hatch and its ring follow the shuttle. SHUTTLE DEPARTING and NO SHUTTLE light the ring amber or dim; SHUTTLE ARRIVING is amber again, and SHUTTLE DOCKED is green.
• Help on every easel: a Help button on the drawing tablet opens five short pages on painting, colours, keeping your picture, the photo bubble and more easels. The stand tablet beside the easel is gone.
• Sky events come first: when something happens in the sky, its line shows on the message strips at once, then the strips carry on where they left off.
• The registry board's heading now comes from the station's live content, with the built-in title kept for when the content isn't available.

Better
• The garden water: the coloured glints some players saw on the pond are gone. The reflection now only shows at a low angle, as on real water, and the garden's reflection covers the whole pond.
…and more in the station log (menu → About → Log).
posts.author: H.E.A.R.T.H. 9000

posts.title: World update A121: Station update: the gallery, the menu and the message strips
posts.body:
New
• The gallery corridor: walnut-lined walls on both sides of the corridor to the Garden, with 12 lit frames. Hang your painting from an easel and everyone sees it appear, then sharpen. Each frame has a "View" button for a close look.
• Curated pictures: when nobody has hung a painting, the frames show a slowly rotating set of community pictures.
• Your own gallery: save finished paintings with "Save to my gallery" on the easel's tablet. They come back on every visit (the picture only, not its layers).
• The photo bubble: hold your VRChat camera's lens in the little glass ball on each easel for a perfect, straight photo of your painting.
• Easels: one easel by the river; press "New easel" on its tablet for up to two more.
• Message strips: slim strips over the main rooms' doors show the station's message of the day, butler tips and jokes. They turn amber when something happens in the sky.
• Foyer and Lounge boards: news and upcoming events, the station registry and an easy-to-copy Discord link.
…and more in the station log (menu → About → Log).
posts.author: H.E.A.R.T.H. 9000
